cases.what: A full index as the publisher writes it: a default entry, entries with a manifest, every optional field present in one entry and absent in another, a name and a summary at the 60-character cap, non-ASCII text, a port, and one block for each reason (with and without an id).
The same index published a day earlier. Valid by itself; a reader that has applied `valid` must refuse it (the rollback floor).
The shape of the first real index: one default entry and an empty blocklist.

An index from a later publisher: an unknown field at the top, in an add-on and in a block. Unknown fields are ignored (plan 1.3), so a reader accepts it. This publisher never writes it, and refuses it as a source.
A lossless.json signed with the same key, served as the index. The signature is good; it has no `type`.
A well-formed index whose `type` is another word.
The bytes of `valid`, signed with a different P-256 key (an unknown key). Only the signature is wrong.
The bytes of `valid` with one byte changed (bad.example became bae.example), with `valid`'s signature.
65 add-ons: one over the cap of 64. Each entry is fine by itself.
257 blocks: one over the cap of 256. Each entry is fine by itself.
A body over the 65536-byte cap: 256 blocks (within the count cap) on long host names.
A block whose `reason` is not one of harmful, broken, impersonation.
